common_name: Kay Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (Near-Black Iris with Mustard Beards)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Kay is a miniature dwarf bearded iris bred by Thomas Johnson and introduced in 2017, prized for flowers that come about as close to true black as the class gets, set off by bold mustard-yellow beards. Johnson named the cultivar for his great-aunt, whose favorite color was black. At under eight inches tall it suits rock gardens and raised beds where taller bearded iris would overwhelm the display. Plant its rhizomes shallowly in full sun with sharp drainage, since the miniature dwarf class is especially sensitive to wet, heavy soil.

common_name: Ribbit Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (Lime Green Iris with Powder-Blue Beards)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Ribbit is a Thomas Johnson miniature dwarf bearded iris from 2020 with wide, rounded light lime-green standards and slightly lighter green falls marked by a small medium-green spot and narrow edge. The beards are tipped powder blue, an unusual color combination for the class that makes the flowers easy to pick out in a mixed dwarf iris bed. It blooms early in the median iris season on stems under eight inches tall, growing into vigorous, floriferous clumps. Give it full sun and sharply drained soil, since miniature dwarf bearded iris rhizomes rot quickly if left wet.

common_name: Tiny Clown Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (Peach-and-Violet Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Tiny Clown, registered by Thomas Johnson in 2019, is a lightly fragrant miniature dwarf bearded iris with standards blending peach and pink over reddish-violet falls softened by a lighter peach zone around tangerine beards. Its playful, bright coloring and compact seven-inch height make it a good candidate for the front of a rock garden or trough planting. Like other median dwarf classes it needs full sun and gritty, fast-draining soil to avoid rhizome rot. Divide congested clumps every few years to keep bloom quality high.

common_name: Twinkle Little Star Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (White-and-Indigo Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Twinkle Little Star is a Paul Black miniature dwarf bearded iris from 2020 that pairs crisp white standards, bands, and darts with white beards against dark indigo falls, giving the flower unusually strong contrast for such a small bloom. The high-contrast pattern reads well from a distance despite the plant's seven-inch stature, making it stand out in mass dwarf-iris plantings. Grow it in full sun with sharp drainage and divide every two to three years as clumps thicken. Its cream styles add a subtle extra layer of color inside the bloom.

common_name: Neon Flash Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (Hot Pink Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Neon Flash is a 2023 Paul Black miniature dwarf bearded iris with saturated mid-to-dark pink standards, darker pink styles, and peach-pink falls that blush rose near clear pink beards. The intensely bright color lives up to the name and makes the thumbnail-sized blooms visible from across a bed despite their small size. Like other members of this class it tops out well under eight inches and needs full sun and sharp drainage to perform reliably. It flowers in the middle-to-late part of the dwarf iris season, helping extend median iris color.

common_name: Happy Elf Miniature Dwarf Bearded Iris (Yellow Bitone Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Happy Elf, a Paul Black introduction from 2025, produces mid-to-dark yellow bitone flowers whose brightness belies the plant's tiny seven-inch stature. Black bred it from a cross involving 'Peach Medley' and a 'Whoa!' sibling, continuing his long run of miniature dwarf bearded introductions. Its scale suits rock gardens and container plantings where larger bearded iris would be out of proportion. As with all MDB iris, plant the rhizomes shallowly in full sun and sharply drained soil to prevent rot.

common_name: Alaia Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Tangerine-Bearded Bicolor Plicata Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Alaia is a standard dwarf bearded iris bred by Thomas Johnson, introduced in 2018 and named for his dog, with a bright, clean bicolor plicata pattern set off by shocking tangerine beards. It won the Walther Cup in 2021, an American Iris Society award recognizing outstanding seedlings and new introductions, and has also proven to be a strong breeding parent. Clumps grow to about thirteen inches on vigorous, three-bud stems. Plant it in full sun with sharp drainage in late summer so it can establish before the standard dwarf bearded season the following spring.

common_name: Atom Smasher Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Golden Yellow-and-Cranberry Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Atom Smasher is a 2021 Thomas Johnson standard dwarf bearded iris with brilliant golden-yellow standards veined red at the edges, paired with falls that carry a near-solid cranberry overlay on a yellow-orange ground around saturated tangerine beards. The high-contrast pattern was bred from a cross with 'Alaia' and forms especially dense, showy clumps at about fourteen inches tall. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained soil, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer for bloom the following spring. Its bold coloring makes it a strong landscape accent among other dwarf bearded iris.

common_name: Blue Eyed Girl Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Honey Yellow Iris with Violet Beards)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Blue Eyed Girl is a Thomas Johnson standard dwarf bearded iris from 2017 with honey-yellow standards over lighter falls washed in deeper honey yellow around bushy, deep violet beards. It earned an SDB Award of Merit from the American Iris Society in 2021, one step in the multi-year award sequence that precedes the class's Cook-Douglas Medal. Strong three-bud stems reach about fifteen inches, near the upper end for the class. Plant it in full sun with sharp drainage in late summer for bloom the following spring.

common_name: Carrot Flash Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Orange-Bearded Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Carrot Flash is a Paul Black standard dwarf bearded iris introduced in 2017, bred as a sibling to 'Festive Bow' and valued for its cute, compact flowers topped with big, flaming orange beards. At around eleven inches tall it sits toward the shorter end of the SDB class, blooming from early to late in the dwarf iris season. Give it full sun and sharply drained soil, setting rhizomes shallowly in late summer so clumps are established before winter. Its small scale and vivid beard color suit rock gardens and border edges.

common_name: Cat's Eye Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Mauve Rose Iris with Red Fall Spot)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Cat's Eye, bred by Paul Black and introduced in 2002, is a standard dwarf bearded iris in mauve-rose with a large, vivid red spot on each fall that gives the flower its name and its striking, unmistakable look. It became one of the most decorated standard dwarf bearded iris of its era, winning the Walther Cup, the Lankow Medal, and the American Iris Society's Cook-Douglas Medal, and finishing as a runner-up for the Dykes Medal across all iris classes. Plants reach about fifteen inches and bloom in midseason among sharply drained, full-sun beds. Its popularity as both a garden plant and breeding parent has kept it widely grown decades after its introduction.

common_name: Oh Canada Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Large-Spotted Bicolor Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Oh Canada is a Thomas Johnson standard dwarf bearded iris from 2015, bred from 'Riveting' crossed with 'Capiche', known for unusually large flowers and bold spotting above neatly two-toned beards. Its wide falls and colorful clumping habit make it stand out early in the dwarf bearded season, on stems around thirteen inches tall. Like other SDB iris, it needs full sun and sharp drainage, with rhizomes planted shallowly in late summer ahead of spring bloom. The strong patterning has made it a popular garden plant among newer Johnson introductions.

common_name: Nickel Intermediate Bearded Iris (Butter-and-Violet Plicata Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Nickel is a Paul Black intermediate bearded iris registered in 2006, with an unusual plicata pattern of butter-yellow standards banded wide in violet and white falls banded narrowly in blue-grape, carried on well-branched, lightly ruffled stems about twenty-six inches tall. The American Iris Society awarded it an Honorable Mention in 2008 and an Award of Merit in 2010, recognition steps on the path toward the class's Williamson-White Medal. Its complex, multi-generation breeding line draws on numerous Black-line seedlings going back to the 1980s. Grow it in full sun with sharp drainage, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer for bloom the following spring.

common_name: Fluffy Kitty Intermediate Bearded Iris (White Glaciata Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Fluffy Kitty is a 2022 Paul Black intermediate bearded iris with a pronounced sweet fragrance and a sparkling white glaciata pattern, its bright yellow hafts and marigold beards catching the light against the pale petals. Bred as a sibling to 'Impressive', it forms dense clumps on stems around twenty-five inches tall with two branches and five to six buds each. As with other intermediate bearded iris, plant the rhizomes shallowly in full sun and sharply drained soil in late summer. Its fragrance and clean coloring make it a good choice near seating areas or garden paths.

common_name: Lumistreak Intermediate Bearded Iris (Broken-Color Luminata Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Lumistreak is a spicy-fragrant Paul Black intermediate bearded iris from 2022 showing a broken-color luminata pattern: beetroot standards blending to butter margins and randomly streaked white, over dark wine falls that shift to bright yellow luminata patches rimmed in gilt gold. The streaked, mischievous patterning sets it apart from more conventional intermediate bearded color classes. Plants reach about twenty-seven inches and need the same full sun and sharp drainage as other median bearded iris. Its unusual coloring makes it a conversation piece in a mixed iris border.

common_name: Caramel Craving Intermediate Bearded Iris (Gold-and-Maroon Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Caramel Craving is a 2025 Thomas Johnson intermediate bearded iris with a slight fragrance, deep golden-yellow standards flushed maroon at the center, and falls in matching deep gold marked by a large maroon spot. Bred from 'Searing Embers' crossed with 'Mind Blowing', it carries a dramatic, high-contrast pattern onto a reliable garden plant about twenty-three inches tall. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained soil, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer for bloom the following spring. The bold spotting reads clearly even at a distance in the garden.

common_name: Boundless Berry Border Bearded Iris (Warm Pink Ruffled Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Boundless Berry is a 2021 Paul Black border bearded iris bred to counter the class's reputation for sparse bloom, producing robust, heavily ruffled light warm-pink flowers on well-branched stems with seven to nine buds. The fall hafts are rouged red-plum and veined cream, shading out to narrower warm-pink bands around big, dark sienna beards, and the blooms carry a moderate sweet fragrance. At roughly twenty-seven inches it has the tall-bearded-type flower proportioned onto a shorter border bearded stem. Plant it in full sun with sharp drainage in late summer for a showy display the following spring.

common_name: Gay Romance Border Bearded Iris (Reverse Purple Amoena Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Gay Romance is a Paul Black border bearded iris from 2020 with a richly saturated reverse amoena pattern -- deep purple standards over paler falls -- accented by tangerine beards. Late in the border bearded season it produces well-branched stands with two branches and seven buds, forming striking clumps. As with other border bearded iris, it needs full sun and sharply drained soil, with rhizomes set shallowly in late summer. Its intense, deeply saturated purple tone is uncommon among reverse amoena patterns in this class.

common_name: Blazing Orange Border Bearded Iris (Fiery Apricot Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Blazing Orange is a sweetly fragrant 2023 Paul Black border bearded iris in fiery apricot-orange, with dark plum hafts setting off vivid red-orange beards. Show stalks carry three branches and eight to nine buds, and the plant quickly builds into dense, eye-catching clumps around twenty-six inches tall. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained soil, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer ahead of spring bloom. Its saturated color makes it one of the brighter orange tones available in the border bearded class.

common_name: Gold Jewelry Border Bearded Iris (Deep Gold Ruffled Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Gold Jewelry is a 2025 Paul Black border bearded iris with a slight sweet fragrance, carrying perfectly proportioned, heavily ruffled deep-gold flowers with marigold beards visible from across a garden. Its strong branching and sturdy twenty-seven-inch stems reflect Black's long breeding focus on improving border bearded iris form and vigor. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun and sharply drained soil in late summer for bloom the following spring. The clean gold tone and refined form make it a strong newer addition to the class.

common_name: Loki Miniature Tall Bearded Iris (Butter Yellow-and-Plum Purple Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Loki is a tetraploid miniature tall bearded iris bred by Lynda Miller and introduced in 2022, named for the Norse trickster god, with deep butter-yellow standards tinted purple at the base above medium plum-purple falls edged in a paler rim and set off by old-gold beards. Its well-branched stems carry ten to fourteen buds, an unusually heavy bud count for the miniature tall bearded class, and reach about twenty inches. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained soil, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer for bloom the following season. The slender, grass-like foliage and proportionate flowers are the hallmark of well-bred miniature tall bearded iris.

common_name: Soft Kitty Miniature Tall Bearded Iris (Orchid Pink-and-Purple Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Soft Kitty is a 2022 Lynda Miller tetraploid miniature tall bearded iris with orchid-pink standards and light purple falls marked by a plum-purple center stripe, pink hafts, and pink-coral beards. Stems can carry up to seventeen buds, giving long-lasting clumps of soft-colored bloom at about twenty-three inches. As with other miniature tall bearded iris, the proportionately small, grass-like form distinguishes it from full-size tall bearded iris sharing similar coloring. Plant it in full sun with sharp drainage in late summer for bloom the following spring.

common_name: Marionberry Miniature Tall Bearded Iris (Smoky Violet-and-Purple Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Marionberry is a 2024 Lynda Miller miniature tall bearded iris with domed, smoky medium-violet standards over dark purple falls marked with cream lines at the haft and a gold beard. Unscented but strongly patterned, it grows to about twenty-three inches on slender, proportionate stems typical of the miniature tall bearded class. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun and sharply drained soil in late summer so clumps establish before the following season's bloom. Its dark, smoky coloring is a departure from the brighter tones common among Miller's other median introductions.

common_name: Maid Of Gold Miniature Tall Bearded Iris (Bright Yellow Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Maid Of Gold is a 2025 Paul Black miniature tall bearded iris with a slight spicy fragrance and lilting, bright mid-yellow flowers and beards throughout, grown on well-branched stems with two branches plus a spur and seven to eight buds. The heavy bud count and clean, all-yellow coloring make it a strong landscape plant for mass display, reaching about twenty-three inches tall. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained soil, planting rhizomes shallowly in late summer for bloom the following spring. Its uniform color sets it apart from more patterned miniature tall bearded introductions.
